To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
seeing another person's direct gaze results in autonomic arousal and approach-related motivational activity in the frontal EEG, and that a smile enhances these effects.
eye contact with a smiling face results in enhanced autonomic arousal and greater relative left-sided activity in the alpha-band, which are both associated with approach motivation.

eye contact with another person, compared to seeing an averted gaze, results in enhanced autonomic arousal and greater relative left-sided activity in the alpha-band of the frontal EEG, associated with approach motivation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of eye contact on autonomic arousal and approach motivation.
the question of how the perception of a direct vs. of an averted gaze is processed and what the consequences are for the individual's autonomic and cortical arousal.
the role of eye contact in human social interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results are in line with the notion that direct gaze is associated with approach motivation, but that this effect may be enhanced by smiling faces.
a smile enhances the effect of direct gaze on autonomic arousal, but not on frontal EEG alpha-band power.
eye contact, in general, enhances autonomic arousal and, in particular, the approach motivation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
seeing direct gaze elicits stronger autonomic responses and greater relative left-sided frontality than does seeing averted gaze.
the autonomic arousal and EEG frontal alpha-band asymmetry responses to eye contact are affected by the facial expression.
the effect of eye contact on autonomic responses is more pronounced in the presence of a smile than a neutral expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
eye contact is a powerful signal of social approach motivation and that this signal is modulated by facial expressions.
